front: In AWS KMS, a team must control who can use a key and see each use of it in CloudTrail. Which key type fits?
back: A customer managed key with its own key policy.
extra: Customer managed keys are keys [you create, own, and manage](../facts/kms.md#kms-customer-managed-key-full-control), and their use goes to your [CloudTrail customer trail or event data store](../facts/kms.md#kms-key-type-logging-owned-not-viewable).

front: In AWS KMS, can an IAM policy allow use of a key whose key policy does not allow IAM policies?
back: No. The key policy decides first.
extra: Without that permission in the key policy, [IAM policies that allow permissions have no effect](../facts/kms.md#kms-iam-policy-allow-needs-key-policy). [The default key policy enables IAM policies](../facts/kms.md#kms-iam-policy-allow-needs-key-policy).

front: In AWS KMS, the waiting period before a key is deleted is {{c1::7 – 30 days}}.
AWS KMS or AWS CloudHSM: which one gives you a single-tenant HSM cluster in your VPC?
extra: CloudHSM gives you a [single-tenant HSM cluster](../facts/cloudhsm.md#cloudhsm-vs-kms-faq-single-tenant-vpc-exclusive). AWS KMS keys also sit in HSMs validated at [FIPS 140-3 Security Level 3](../facts/kms.md#kms-hsm-fips-140-3-level-3).

front: In AWS KMS, the Encrypt operation takes plaintext of up to {{c1::4 KB}}.
extra: For larger data, use envelope encryption with a data key.

front: In AWS KMS, automatic rotation of a customer managed key with no rotation period set happens every {{c1::365 days}}.
In AWS KMS, a custom automatic rotation period is {{c1::between 90 and 2560 days}}.
In AWS CloudHSM, high availability is automatic when a cluster has {{c1::at least two HSMs}} across Availability Zones.
In AWS KMS, can you convert an existing single-Region key into a multi-Region key?
back: No. Create a new multi-Region key and re-encrypt.
extra: [You cannot convert a single-Region key](../facts/kms.md#kms-mrk-cannot-convert) to a multi-Region key, so [you must re-encrypt your data](../facts/kms.md#kms-mrk-cannot-convert) under the new key.

front: In Amazon RDS, can you share a DB snapshot that is encrypted with the AWS managed key?
extra: You [can't share a snapshot](../facts/kms.md#kms-rds-aws-managed-key-snapshot-no-share) that is [encrypted using the AWS managed key](../facts/kms.md#kms-rds-aws-managed-key-snapshot-no-share) of the sharing account.

front: In AWS KMS, a disabled key or a deleted key: which one can you use again later?
back: The disabled key. A deleted key cannot be recovered.
extra: When you are not sure, AWS suggests [disabling the KMS key instead of deleting it](../facts/kms.md#kms-disable-instead-of-delete), because [you cannot recover a deleted KMS key](../facts/kms.md#kms-disable-instead-of-delete).

front: In AWS KMS, a recovery Region must decrypt data during a Region outage without a cross-Region call. Which key?
back: A multi-Region key with a replica in the recovery Region.
extra: Related multi-Region keys have [the same key material and key ID](../facts/kms.md#kms-mrk-same-material-no-cross-region-call), so the recovery Region decrypts [without re-encrypting or making a cross-Region call](../facts/kms.md#kms-mrk-same-material-no-cross-region-call).
